sources.claim: Incubation (setting a problem aside) improves later insight in lab studies
A sealed, device-only idea log helps people return to ideas fresh
Bach-y-Rita 1969: camera image projected onto the skin of the back (tactile vision substitution)
Meijer 1992: image-to-sound encoding (The vOICe)
Substitution used to anticipate a lead vehicle (preprint pointed to by @seeingwithsound, 2026-09-30)
A closed glyph code (bar, gap, stack) read by sight or tone gives the same sum: agreement, not acuity
Augmentative and alternative communication (AAC): people communicate intent without speech, using gestures, symbols and switch patterns
Morse code: a two-element timing code (short / long) carries meaning by pattern alone
Non-lexical sounds (uh-huh, mm) carry conversational intent without words
A small personal tap vocabulary is faster than typing for a few frequent intents
The Page Visibility API reports when a page is hidden (another tab or app) and visible again
Gloria Mark's studies: average attention on one screen before switching fell to about 47 seconds
Seeing your own unbroken stretches helps you hold longer ones
DeviceOrientation events report device tilt (beta = front-to-back) and iOS requires an explicit permission request
Tilt-to-scroll was studied as a one-handed reading technique on handhelds (Rekimoto 1996, Tilting operations for small screen interfaces)
A gesture that is off by default and shows its own reading is trusted more than an always-on one
Negative mean asynchrony: people tapping along to a metronome tend to tap tens of milliseconds before the beat
Sensorimotor synchronization research reviews (Repp 2005; Repp & Su 2013)
Seeing your own lead/lag after a round makes the next round steadier
Benchmark floor and skill count over 22 hours, read from this repo's git history (tools/bench.best.json, void-live-deploy/skills/index.json)
Pearson correlation measures linear co-movement, not cause
More skills cause a higher benchmark (rather than both following the same agents' rounds)
35 pull requests merged into atomeam/void-loop on 2026-10-03, by branch lane (claude 12, helper 12, grok 10, forethinkers 1)
The breaks listed (key reaching the answer model, a skill collision, append conflicts, stalled runs) and their fixes
More parallel lanes raised output, and checks can absorb the conflict cost
Inverse document frequency (Sparck Jones 1972): a term in few documents carries more information
The 27 agent log lines of 2026-10-03, ranked by their average rare-word weight
The rarest lines of a day are the ones worth a person's attention
Rising final pitch commonly marks questions and continuation; falling pitch marks statements and finality (intonation in English)
Autocorrelation estimates the fundamental frequency of a voiced sound (de Cheveigné & Kawahara, YIN)
A one-second hum contour (rising / falling / level) is a usable yes / no / wait signal for a person who would rather not speak or type
Void routes an ask to the first ability in skills/index.json whose match() takes it; abilities list nearMisses they must refuse (tools/skills-check.mjs)
Showing people why a system made a decision (explanation interfaces) helps them predict and correct it
Seeing who would answer before asking turns would-be misses into asks people rephrase, so fewer reach the miss board
The Brier score, the mean squared gap between a stated probability and what happened, measures forecast quality; always saying 50% scores 0.25
People who keep score of their probabilistic forecasts become better calibrated over time (Good Judgment Project)
Scoring your own hunches tells you which of your weak signals are worth acting on
Incubation (setting an unsolved problem aside) improves problem solving on average; a meta-analysis of 117 studies found a reliable but modest effect
Sleep between attempts more than doubled the rate of discovering a hidden shortcut in a number task
Writing a stuck problem down at night and revisiting it the next day helps this person, measured by their own hit rate
The psychomotor vigilance task (reacting to a counter shown at random 2-10 s intervals) is a standard, practice-resistant measure of sustained attention
Lapses (reactions of 500 ms or more) on the vigilance task rise steadily with chronic sleep restriction, even when people rate themselves as only slightly sleepy
A short 2-minute home version, logged by time of day, shows when this person is sharpest

Duration judgments differ by paradigm: when people know in advance they will judge time (prospective) their estimates behave differently from when they are asked only afterwards (retrospective), and mental load shifts the two in opposite directions (meta-analysis)
Time that was full of events tends to be remembered as longer, while it often feels shorter while it is happening (the holiday paradox)
When this person knows in advance they will be asked (they mark the start), their duration estimates are biased in a steady direction that depends on whether they were busy or idle
A camera image turned into sound (left to right in time, height as pitch, brightness as loudness) can convey pictures to the ear; this is the design of The vOICe
Blind people trained with a tactile vision-substitution system learned to recognise objects and their layout through touch on the skin
With practice, this person can tell simple shapes apart by sound alone, measured as a hit rate above the 1-in-4 chance level
People using decision aids tend to accept automated suggestions without enough checking (automation bias), including wrong ones, across fields such as aviation and medicine
In clinical decision support, automation bias raised errors when advice was wrong; committing to one's own judgment before seeing the advice is among the suggested mitigations
This person catches more wrong suggestions when they answer before seeing the suggestion than when they see it first
A simple template matcher (resample, rotate, scale, compare) recognizes single-stroke gestures with about 97% accuracy from one example per shape, and 99% with three or more
Gesture-only interfaces hurt usability when gestures are invisible and undiscoverable and give no feedback; an equivalent visible control and clear feedback are recommended
This person's own strokes are read right at least 90% of the time after 20 tries, so drawing could stand in for these four buttons for them
People neglect base rates when judging how likely something is from a specific description (representativeness)
In a large geopolitical forecasting tournament, brief training in probabilistic reasoning (including starting from base rates) made forecasts more accurate
For this person, starting from a base rate and weighing each signal explicitly gives better-scored chances than their gut, over 15 or more resolved hunches
An undemanding task during an incubation break led to more new ideas on a repeated unusual-uses problem than a demanding task, rest, or no break
Incubation effects vary with the kind of problem and what fills the break; a meta-analysis of 117 studies found the effect is larger for divergent (many-answer) problems
For this person, an easy task in the break gives more new ideas than a hard task or rest, measured by their own rounds
Of the UAP reports US officials could resolve, most were ordinary objects such as balloons, birds, drones, aircraft and satellites
Low-orbit satellites, including Starlink, are visible when the observer's sky is dark but the satellite is still sunlit, which concentrates sightings in the hours around dusk and dawn
Checking a personal sighting against the sun's position and a short list of common explanations resolves most of what a person logs
When two targets appear in a rapid stream, the second is often missed if it comes about 200-500 ms after the first, and caught at shorter or longer gaps (the attentional blink)
The blink has been repeated widely and varies between people; second-target accuracy is usually measured only on trials where the first target was reported
A person's own blink can be seen with a few dozen home trials at a handful of gaps, though browser frame timing makes it rougher than a lab's
Blind people trained with a tactile vision substitution system learned to recognise objects and their positions through touch
The vOICe maps image height to pitch and left-right position to time and stereo, and users can learn to read images from sound
A person's miss distance on this two-cue sound task (pitch for height, stereo for side) shrinks over a few dozen trials at home
Signal detection theory separates sensitivity (d') from response bias (criterion) in yes/no detection, so a listener who says yes more often is not scored as hearing better
The log-linear correction (add 0.5 to counts, 1 to totals) keeps hit and false-alarm rates of 0 or 1 usable and biases d' less than other fixes
A 2-down 1-up staircase settles near the level where about 71% of signals are detected
A person's own d' for a faint tone in hiss, measured at home with ordinary headphones over about 30 trials, is stable enough to compare day to day
People judging correlation from scatterplots tend to underestimate moderate correlations, and judgments improve toward r = 1
Perceived correlation in scatterplots follows a consistent law across observers, with the largest underestimation at middle values
A person's own middle-band underestimate can be seen in about twenty guesses on a phone screen
People match a made-up word like 'maluma' to a rounded shape and 'takete' to a jagged one far more often than chance
The bouba-kiki match holds across speakers of 25 languages and 10 writing systems, though more weakly in some
Voiceless stops and front vowels lean 'sharp', and sonorants with back rounded vowels lean 'round'
A person's own match rate with randomly built words and randomly drawn shapes, over a few dozen rounds, is clearly above 50%
With a large enough number of chances, any outrageous thing is likely to happen (the law of truly large numbers); many striking coincidences have ordinary explanations
The chance of at least one event in n independent tries, each with chance p, is 1 - (1 - p)^n
Seeing their own chance-only count lowers how much weight people give a single striking coincidence
When people cause a tone by a voluntary key press, the felt gap between press and tone is shorter than when the same events are not self-caused (intentional binding)
Intentional binding is widely used as an implicit measure of the sense of agency, though what it measures is debated
A browser version with a machine-initiated press as the comparison shows the same direction of effect in about 20 trials per condition

When people reproduce time intervals drawn from a range, their reproductions are pulled toward the middle of that range: short intervals are overestimated and long ones underestimated (central tendency, Vierordt's law)
The variability of timed responses grows roughly in proportion to the interval being timed (the scalar property)
Seeing their own slope below 1 helps people notice that their sense of duration is pulled toward recent experience
Flying-bomb hits on south London, believed to be aimed at particular districts, fitted a random (Poisson) distribution
People see streaks and clusters in random sequences and read them as meaningful (the clustering illusion)
Comparing a personal log of odd events against same-size random timelines changes how much people read into a run of events
